title: Week of 11/23/2026: VIX® Jumps to 1-Year High, but No Panic as AI Trade Unwinds
summary: Friday’s VIX® move, while large, was surprisingly orderly. The sell-off in SPX® spot (-3.7%) and the increase in fixed-strike vols (+3.2 pts) accounted for almost 90% of the 7.4pt VIX increase. Learn more in this week’s Macro Volatility Digest.
author: Mandy Xu
text:
Week of 11/23/2026: VIX® Jumps to 1-Year High, but No Panic as AI Trade Unwinds
Friday’s VIX ® move, while large, was surprisingly orderly. The sell-off in SPX ® spot (-3.7%) and the increase in fixed-strike vols (+3.2 pts) accounted for almost 90% of the 7.4pt VIX increase. Very little came from demand for downside puts. In fact, changes in skew and convexity contributed just 0.9pt to the VIX move (see chart below). In contrast, demand for downside protection made up almost half of the Nov 5th VIX spike. This can also be seen in measures of SPX 1M skew (25-delta ratio), which spiked to the 95th percentile high after the Nov 5th sell-off but only steepened modestly to the 80th percentile last Friday.
While implied vols rose across every asset class, equity vol far outpaced the rest, suggesting the rise in equity risk was more a story of equity positioning than broad macro de-risking. Single stock vol jumped more than index vol, in another sign Friday’s move was more about idiosyncratic risk (e.g. the AI theme), rather than macro risk. Notably, expected stock dispersion increased on Friday, with the DSPX SM index rising 5 pts to 42%. This comes as investors rotate out of the AI theme into other sectors, rather than selling everything indiscriminately.
As tech stocks fall out of favor, Tech vols have risen the most, with QQQ 1M implied vol jumping over 20 pts last week, the most of any global index. In contrast, US small cap volatility, which has very little exposure to the AI theme, saw its volatility trail that of its large-cap counterparts. The RTY-SPX 1M implied vol spread narrowed to a 6-year low of 1.4% as a result.
